agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider West Sells Park signage and speed bumps request
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a request from a resident, Aleyna Golinsky, about adding signage and speed bumps at West Sells Park. The item was referred from the Community Consultation Committee meeting held on May 26, 2026, and now appears on the council agenda with three attached photos of the park. Council has not yet decided whether to approve the signage or the speed bumps. If approved, new traffic-calming measures and signs could be installed near the park, which may affect how vehicles move through nearby streets.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision if your business or deliveries use streets near West Sells Park.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider crosswalk across North Road at Still Creek Avenue
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a request from Connie Elder to add a crosswalk, ideally with a light, across North Road at Still Creek Avenue. The request was referred from the May 26, 2026 Community Consultation Process. Elder notes North Road traffic has become busier and faster with new development, making it harder for Sullivan Heights and Oakdale residents to reach shopping and SkyTrain. She also requests a crosswalk at Clarke Road, noting no crosswalks exist across North Road between Broadway and Casewell Street. No decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision — a new crosswalk could change traffic and pedestrian access near your business.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Union Street traffic calming request
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a resident's request for traffic calming measures on the 3700 block of Union Street, a steep stretch leading to the Union and Boundary Road intersection. The request, from Christian Chiappetta, was referred from the Community Consultation Panel meeting on July 14, 2026, and includes photos of a student driver and cyclists. Council has not yet decided whether to approve any changes. If approved, new measures like speed bumps, signage, or lane changes could affect traffic flow and access for businesses on or near Union Street.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on Union Street traffic calming — it could affect traffic and access to your business.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider HUB Cycling amendments to Burnaby Street and Traffic Bylaw 1961
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council has passed Section 18D(3) of the Street and Traffic Bylaw 1961, banning electric kick scooters on the Major Road Network and minor and major arterial roads unless riders are in a protected cycle lane or multi-use pathway. The ban goes beyond provincial Electric Kick Scooter Pilot Program rules, despite Burnaby joining the pilot in January 2026. HUB Cycling warns the restriction affects key business corridors like Kingsway, Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue, and is urging Council to fast-track protected cycling infrastructure.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If your business relies on arterial-road access, review how the e-scooter ban on the Major Road Network affects customers and deliveries.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider regional micro-mobility share network proposal
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a proposal from Markus Lau to build a regional micro-mobility share network — a shared system of e-bikes and e-scooters that people can rent for short trips. The item was referred from the July 28, 2026 Community and Corporate Planning Committee and is now on the council agenda. No decisions have been made yet. If approved, the network could bring new rules for where these devices can be parked, ridden, and operated in Burnaby. Businesses that rent or sell bikes and scooters, or that rely on sidewalks and parking areas, may want to follow the discussion.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision and any proposed rules for shared e-bikes and e-scooters in Burnaby.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider bus and bike lane conflict on 145 Route
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a delegation item referred from the July 28, 2026 Community and Civic Planning meeting about a conflict zone between bus and bike lanes on the 145 Route. HUB Cycling Burnaby raised the issue, and Council is set to review the referral at an upcoming meeting. No decision has been made yet, and no bylaw or rule change has been approved. If Council decides to act, it could lead to changes in how the 145 Route is designed or used, which may affect traffic, parking, or access along that corridor.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on the 145 Route lane conflict — it could affect traffic and access along that corridor.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider sidewalk request for Alaska St, Rosser Ave, Juneau St
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider resident Helen Luketic's third request since 2022 for sidewalks on Alaska Street, Rosser Avenue and Juneau Street, referred from the Community Consultation Panel on September 8, 2026. The corridor serves over 644 occupied homes in the Alaska, Bordeaux, Juneau and Tailor developments, with pedestrians including children walking to Kitchener Elementary using the roadway. No decision has been made; staff would likely study the area and report back on cost, design and timing. Sidewalk work can affect parking, driveway access and street frontage for nearby businesses.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If your business sits on or near these streets, watch for the council decision and any staff report on sidewalk construction.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Kensington Avenue signal changes at Joe Sakic Way
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a resident's request for a formal operational review of the two closely spaced traffic signals on Kensington Avenue at Joe Sakic Way and the Christine Sinclair Community Centre access. The request asks staff to report on signal timing and detector logic, traffic volumes, queue lengths and delays, whether the two signals are coordinated, how quickly a minor-approach vehicle or pedestrian call can interrupt Kensington traffic, and planned signal upgrades tied to the new Burnaby Lake Recreation Centre. No decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision and any public consultation on the Kensington Avenue signal changes.
